title: PREP Act COVID-19 Declaration coverage for qualified pharmacy technicians who administer vaccines
subtopic: Federal PREP Act coverage for technician vaccine administration
rule_summary: The Declaration Under the Public Readiness and Emergency Preparedness Act for Medical Countermeasures Against COVID-19, as amended and republished in full by its 12th Amendment (89 FR 99875, December 11, 2024, effective January 1, 2025), identifies in section V(d) as qualified persons the pharmacy interns and qualified pharmacy technicians who administer, if the intern or technician acts under the supervision of a State-licensed pharmacist and is licensed or registered by his or her State board of pharmacy, (1) vaccines that CDC/ACIP recommend to persons ages three through 18 according to CDC's/ACIP's standard immunization schedule, (2) seasonal influenza vaccine that CDC/ACIP recommends to persons aged 19 and older according to that schedule, or (3) FDA-authorized or FDA-licensed COVID-19 vaccines to persons ages three or older. They are qualified persons only if the listed requirements are met, including that the vaccine is authorized, approved, or licensed by the FDA; a COVID-19 vaccination is ordered and administered according to CDC's/ACIP's COVID-19 vaccine recommendations, and a childhood vaccination or a technician-administered seasonal influenza vaccination according to CDC's/ACIP's standard immunization schedule; the supervising pharmacist is readily and immediately available to the immunizing qualified pharmacy technician; the technician has completed a practical training program approved by the ACPE that includes hands-on injection technique, clinical evaluation of indications and contraindications of vaccines, and the recognition and treatment of emergency reactions to vaccines; the technician has a current certificate in basic cardiopulmonary resuscitation; and the technician complies with any applicable requirements (or conditions of use) set forth in the CDC COVID-19 vaccination provider agreement and any other federal requirements that apply to the administration of COVID-19 vaccines. Under section XII(i), liability protections for qualified pharmacy technicians who administer COVID-19 vaccines to individuals aged three and above, CDC/ACIP recommended seasonal influenza vaccines to persons aged three through 18, and seasonal influenza vaccines to individuals aged nineteen and above last through December 31, 2029; other vaccines recommended for persons aged three through 18 are covered for the periods set by other paragraphs of section XII. The amendment states that, to the extent any State law would otherwise prohibit these qualified persons from prescribing, dispensing, or administering Covered Countermeasures that are COVID-19 vaccines, seasonal influenza vaccines or COVID-19 tests, such law is preempted. Sections V(i) and XII(i) separately cover qualified pharmacy technicians who, under the supervision of a State-licensed pharmacist, administer FDA-authorized, approved, or licensed COVID-19 therapeutics subcutaneously, intramuscularly, or orally, on conditions that include a supervising pharmacist readily and immediately available, ACPE-approved practical training for injected therapeutics and a current certificate in basic cardiopulmonary resuscitation; for the therapeutics identified in section VII(d) of the Declaration that coverage lasts through December 31, 2029.
exam_relevance: Tests that the Massachusetts bar on technician vaccine administration in 247 CMR 8.02(6)(d) and 8.04(4)(e) sits beside a time-limited federal overlay: qualified pharmacy technicians are covered for COVID-19 and seasonal influenza vaccination only on the Declaration's conditions and only through December 31, 2029.

numeric_facts.fact: end of PREP Act coverage for qualified pharmacy technicians administering COVID-19 vaccines and seasonal influenza vaccines
numeric_facts.conditions: section XII(i) of the COVID-19 Declaration as amended by the 12th Amendment

numeric_facts.fact: minimum age of a person to whom a qualified pharmacy technician may administer a COVID-19 vaccine under the Declaration
numeric_facts.conditions: FDA-authorized or FDA-licensed COVID-19 vaccine, ordered and administered according to CDC's/ACIP's COVID-19 vaccine recommendations

numeric_facts.conditions: according to CDC's/ACIP's standard immunization schedule

exceptions: Coverage depends on every listed condition, including supervision by a State-licensed pharmacist who is readily and immediately available, ACPE-approved practical training and a current basic cardiopulmonary resuscitation certificate.
The stated coverage for technician-administered COVID-19 and seasonal influenza vaccines ends on December 31, 2029.
common_confusions: The Declaration is a federal liability-immunity instrument with an express preemption statement; it does not amend 247 CMR 8.02(6)(d) or 8.04(4)(e).
The coverage reaches only the countermeasures, ages and conditions the Declaration names, and only for its stated period.
verification_notes: Read in the Federal Register publication of the 12th Amendment (89 FR 99875) on federalregister.gov on 2026-09-11, together with Federal Register searches for later documents on the COVID-19 Declaration, which returned none published after it. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
